rationale: Fresh-eyes code-quality sweep of the five largest non-test diffs at tip 8eaeb05e (internal/complete/complete.go +712, internal/complete/materialize.go +500, internal/next/guard.go +447, cmd/mindspec/next.go +403, internal/gitutil/materialize.go +376), plus internal/phase/{phaselock,semantics_v2}.go and cmd/mindspec/repair.go. Mechanical health is good: `gofmt -l ./cmd ./internal` is clean, `go vet ./...` is clean, and no swallowed errors were introduced outside idiomatic lock-release and cobra `Flags().Get*` positions. Error-handling completeness in the new write-ahead machinery is genuinely disciplined — resolveMaterializationDiscriminator PROPAGATES every git read failure with the rationale stated at each site (fix-round G3), and the S-stage classifies the exact tree it is about to commit (fix-round G1) rather than trusting an earlier read. guard.go's containment rework (toplevelOf / containedRel / resolveContainingDirs) is correct, including the deliberate leaf-unresolved choice that keeps a symlinked .gitignore matchable against porcelain's own tracked name. And the branch IMPROVED the codebase's worst complexity hotspot rather than worsening it: internal/complete.Run went from ~960 lines on main to 877 at the tip despite absorbing new logic, via real extractions (completeSyncPhase, runCommittedRangeGate, handleADRGateOutcome, and the whole materialize.go split). What the targeted per-bead lenses skipped is COMMENT AND DOC TRUTH ACROSS BEAD BOUNDARIES — the class no per-bead panel could see, because each defect was correct when its own bead landed and was falsified by a LATER bead editing a different file. Six such defects are below. Five are stale or wrong prose; one (F2) is a false COMPLETENESS claim in the phase lock's own contract header, which omits both writers this branch's own bead 2 added. None is a hard block and none changes runtime behavior, but in a spec whose entire thesis is that lifecycle surfaces must not assert what the code does not support, shipping a lock header that claims to enumerate EVERY mindspec_phase writer while missing two of them — and a disclosure whose own pointer lands on the wrong function — is the spec failing its own standard in its own source. All six fixes are prose-only and cheap.
concrete_changes_required: F1 cmd/mindspec/next.go: reattach claimFailureError's orphaned doc comment. Bead ta30.8 (7f4ad41b) inserted `readinessOverrideFailure` and its doc comment BETWEEN claimFailureError's doc comment (lines 671-676) and `func claimFailureError` (line 699), with no blank line separating the two comment blocks. Verified with `go doc -all -u ./cmd/mindspec`: readinessOverrideFailure's godoc now opens with 'claimFailureError builds the spec 093 Req 3 claim-failure recovery error for the `mindspec next` ClaimBead caller...', and claimFailureError itself renders with NO doc comment. On main the comment is correctly attached (main:cmd/mindspec/next.go:484-488), so this is a regression this branch introduced. Fix: move the claimFailureError comment block (lines 671-676) down so it sits directly above `func claimFailureError` at line 699.

F2 internal/phase/phaselock.go lines 3-12: the file header claims the lock 'serializes EVERY mindspec_phase writer' and then enumerates them. At the reviewed tip that enumeration is INCOMPLETE — it omits both writers bead 2 added on this very branch: cmd/mindspec/next.go:608 (advancePhaseOnClaim, the claim-path advance) and internal/phase/semantics_v2.go:128 (EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2, the one-shot v2 reconciliation). writer_inventory_test.go enforces the invariant structurally via an AST walk but maintains no list, so this header is the ONLY human-readable inventory and a reader trusting it will miss two writers. Additionally every one of its seven file:line citations now points at unrelated code: plan.go:455 (actual call internal/approve/plan.go:513), spec.go:76 (actual internal/approve/spec.go:203), complete.go:1366 (actual internal/complete/complete.go:1334), release.go:152 (release does not call WithPhaseWriteLock directly at all — it routes through phase.SanctionedDerivedSync, internal/phase/sanctioned_sync.go:53), impl.go:577-579/:611-613 (actual internal/approve/impl.go:587 and :630), adopt.go:424/:437 (actual internal/approve/adopt.go:428), repair.go:189-191 (actual cmd/mindspec/repair.go:254). Fix: add the two missing writers and replace the line numbers with function names, which do not drift.

F3 project-docs/user/guides/lifecycle-modes.md lines 171-181: bead 4 discharged bead 2's routed residual by disclosing it and pointing the reader at 'its own doc comment (`complete.go:1398-1420`)'. That citation was ACCURATE at bead 4's merge (febec324, where completeSyncPhase sat at line 1420) and was falsified by bead 5. At the tip, completeSyncPhase's doc comment is internal/complete/complete.go:1297-1332, while lines 1398-1420 are advanceState's doc comment and say nothing about the residue. The disclosure the bead-4 panel required is therefore broken at the tip: a reader who follows its own pointer finds the wrong function. Fix: cite `completeSyncPhase`'s doc comment in internal/complete/complete.go by NAME, without a line range.

F4 internal/phase/semantics_v2.go line 7: the file header cites "plan.go:462" as the sibling OQ-3 change that made plan-approve write `plan` instead of `implement`. The actual `state.ModePlan` write is internal/approve/plan.go:517; line 462 is an unrelated comment about specID validation. Fix: cite the function (ApprovePlan's phase-write closure) rather than a line number.

F5 internal/complete/complete.go lines 1328-1332 (completeSyncPhase's doc comment): the recorded bead-2 residual still reads as an OPEN action item — 'Routed to beads 4/5 (the agreement-table/result-message work): either fold completeSyncPhase's write through a stored-aware no-op-on-backward guard ... or extend the agreement-table wording to name this fence's honest scope.' Bead 4 took the second option and landed it in project-docs/user/guides/lifecycle-modes.md (the 'Disclosed residual, not silently excepted' paragraph). Both beads are merged, so the routing is discharged but the comment still presents it as pending. Fix: reword to record that the disclosure route was taken and name where it lives.

F6 internal/complete/materialize.go lines 430-434 (sExitContract): the `else if len(knownResidualArtifactDirt) > 0` fallback prints 'WARN complete.residual_artifact_dirt: %v (survived materialization; non-blocking per ADR-0025)' — but it is reached ONLY when the fresh classification on line 423 just found artifactDirt EMPTY. In every state that reaches it the named artifact did NOT survive materialization: either the S-stage committed it into D (the ordinary dirty-artifact path), or CheckDirtyTreeDetail's own `bd export` normalization removed it. So the one branch of this warning that can fire asserts the opposite of what the immediately preceding measurement found — the exact 'message states what the code did not measure' shape AC-4/AC-14 exist to eliminate. Note the only test named for this warning, TestRun_SExitContract_ResidualArtifactDirtWarns (complete_test.go:2794), exercises the FIRST branch, not this one: verified by -coverprofile, that test covers block 430.27-432.3 and leaves 432.47-434.3 at count 0, and no test in the package asserts this fallback's text. Fix: either drop the knownResidualArtifactDirt fallback (the fresh classification at line 423 is already authoritative) or reword it to say what is actually true of the state that reaches it.

findings.title: claimFailureError's doc comment is orphaned onto readinessOverrideFailure (regression vs main)
findings.detail: cmd/mindspec/next.go:671-699. Bead ta30.8 inserted readinessOverrideFailure between claimFailureError's doc comment and its function, with no blank line, so Go attaches the comment to the wrong function. `go doc -all -u ./cmd/mindspec` renders readinessOverrideFailure's documentation beginning 'claimFailureError builds the spec 093 Req 3 claim-failure recovery error...'; claimFailureError itself documents as bare. main:cmd/mindspec/next.go:484-488 has it correctly attached, so the branch introduced this. Prose-only, no behavior change.

findings.title: phaselock.go's 'EVERY mindspec_phase writer' header omits both writers bead 2 added, and all 7 of its line citations are stale
findings.detail: internal/phase/phaselock.go:3-12. Missing from the enumeration: cmd/mindspec/next.go:608 (advancePhaseOnClaim) and internal/phase/semantics_v2.go:128 (EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2) — both new on this branch. Stale citations, each verified by reading the cited line: plan.go:455 -> real call at internal/approve/plan.go:513; spec.go:76 -> internal/approve/spec.go:203; complete.go:1366 -> internal/complete/complete.go:1334; release.go:152 -> release reaches the lock only indirectly via phase.SanctionedDerivedSync (sanctioned_sync.go:53); impl.go:577-579/:611-613 -> internal/approve/impl.go:587 and :630; adopt.go:424/:437 -> internal/approve/adopt.go:428; repair.go:189-191 -> cmd/mindspec/repair.go:254. writer_inventory_test.go is a structural AST walk that keeps no list, so this header is the sole readable inventory. This is the sharpest of the six: it is a false COMPLETENESS claim in the serialization contract's own header, in a spec about not overclaiming.

findings.title: sExitContract's residual-dirt fallback prints a claim contradicted by the measurement that gates it
findings.detail: internal/complete/materialize.go:430-434. The fallback fires only when the fresh classification at line 423 returned an EMPTY artifactDirt, i.e. exactly when the named artifact did NOT survive materialization — it was committed into D, or normalized away by CheckDirtyTreeDetail's own `bd export`. Message says 'survived materialization'. Coverage evidence: TestRun_SExitContract_ResidualArtifactDirtWarns (the only test asserting this warning's text) covers block 430.27-432.3 and leaves 432.47-434.3 at 0; TestBead6Leg_vii_ArtifactByteIdenticalUntilSyncCommit (the ordinary real-git dirty-artifact full run) also leaves it at 0 and emits no such WARN. The block is reached somewhere in the full -short package suite but no test asserts its text.

findings.title: repair.go renders the same two ID positions two different ways inside one switch (pre-existing, not a regression)
findings.detail: cmd/mindspec/repair.go: the `wroteWithForce` leg this branch ADDED (lines 331-332) routes specID/epicID through idrender.Spec/idrender.Bead, while the adjacent 'already consistent' (328-329) and 'repaired' (334-335) legs, the event=lifecycle.phase_repaired line (324-325), and the two `recovery` strings (309, 311) pass both raw. The raw renderings are pre-existing on main (main:cmd/mindspec/repair.go:198,201,204), so this is not a regression and both forms are safe here (specID/epicID are validated upstream). Flagged only because the branch introduced a second convention directly beside the first, so a maintainer now sees two rules in one switch. No change required.

findings.title: next.EntangleableClaimPaths is exported but has no production caller
findings.detail: internal/next/guard.go:60. The exported accessor is referenced only from internal/next/entangle_test.go. Its doc comment already explains it is the test-injectable residual's reader, so this is a deliberate exported-for-tests accessor rather than dead code, but it widens the package's public surface for a test-only need. No change required.

findings.title: Positive: Run shrank while gaining functionality, and the new git primitives are error-honest
findings.detail: internal/complete.Run is 877 lines at the tip vs roughly 960 on main, despite absorbing bead 6's protocol — the branch extracted completeSyncPhase, runCommittedRangeGate and handleADRGateOutcome and moved the whole staged flow into materialize.go. Run remains this codebase's largest single function and a future extraction candidate, but the branch moved it in the right direction rather than the usual accretion. Separately, resolveMaterializationDiscriminator and the S-stage publish path propagate every git read failure instead of degrading to a default classification (CREATE semantics, or clear-and-proceed), each with the hazard named at the site — this is the strongest error-handling discipline in the diff. gofmt and go vet are both clean across ./cmd and ./internal.
